content: We communicate with the user in German; all persisted writing (code, comments, commit messages, issues, documentation) stays in English.

After changing function signatures in the dagmar Dagger module (.dagger/main.go), run dagger develop to regenerate the on-disk client (dagger.gen.go, internal/dagger/*.gen.go). dagger call and dagger functions regenerate internally at RUNTIME, so execution keeps working, but the on-disk generated code and thus gopls/IDE stay stale and report undefined errors on removed functions until dagger develop runs.

dagmar Dagger module layout: dagger.json at the repo root with source=.dagger, code under .dagger/. dagger init --source=.dagger creates .dagger/{main.go, internal/dagger, dagger.gen.go, go.mod, go.sum}. The .dagger dir has its OWN go.mod (module dagger/dagmar) because Go ignores dot-directories in a normal module build, so the Dagger module must be self-contained and isolated from the root github.com/denkhaus/dagmar go.mod (which lives in the shared go.work). The root Go build never sees .dagger/ by design.

Do NOT delete the .dagger generated files (.dagger/dagger.gen.go, .dagger/internal/dagger/). They are git-ignored (not committed) but REQUIRED locally: .dagger/main.go imports the generated client package dagger/dagmar/internal/dagger (uses dagger.K3SOpts, *dagger.K3S, etc.), so deleting them breaks compilation (gopls/IDE shows errors in main.go). They regenerate on every dagger develop/call. On a fresh clone, run dagger develop once to generate them. (Ignoring them is the Dagger convention; committing them is an option but causes git churn on regen.)

Where different kinds of information live (tool-role delineation): (1) Decisions, conventions, patterns, failures, references -> `ml` (Mulch) — durable expertise that surfaces contextually via `ml prime`. (2) Work items, backlog, issues, plans -> `sd` (Seeds) — git-native issue tracker; GitHub holds only code. (3) Transient, cycle- or session-specific detail (e.g. a review-resolution handoff) -> a docs file paired with its artifact (e.g. under `docs/review/`), NOT a permanent `ml` guide. Why: `ml` guides are injected into EVERY session via `ml prime`, so transient content there becomes evergreen noise once the cycle ends. How to apply: reserve `ml` guides for durable, recurring resume instructions (e.g. the Wayfinder resume). For a handoff, split durable vs transient: decision -> `ml`, backlog item -> `sd`, detail -> docs file.

title: Cross-module Go deps under Dagger load: published require (public repo) + GOPRIVATE
rationale: ADR-0014 GAP-1 needed the manifest shared across .dagger/.dagmar. Relative replace fails at load (source isolation — sibling absent from the module load context); a committed vendor/ fails (the SDK's load-time go mod tidy ignores vendor). A published versioned require DOES resolve at load, but only because the dagmar repo is public (Go fetches over HTTPS with no auth — the load container has no git insteadOf/token). GOPRIVATE skips proxy/sumdb for a newly-published module.

description: SYMPTOM: pre-push gate fails fast (~30s) with ubi/mise '403 Forbidden' / 'API rate limit exceeded for <IP>' for dagger/lefthook/golangci-lint/nushell. NOT a code defect — do not chase it as one. Recognize the ubi/mise 403 signature, --no-verify through it, rely on CI.
resolution: INTERIM: push with --no-verify; CI (GitHub Actions, different IP) validates independently. PERMANENT: seed dagmar-233c — inject GITHUB_TOKEN as a Dagger Secret into bootstrap.go (.WithSecretVariable, not plain WithEnvVariable), gate.go takes an optional *dagger.Secret, lefthook.yml + CI pass --github-token env:GITHUB_TOKEN; a gitignored .envrc (direnv) provides the token. Prune this record once 233c lands.
